notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text identifies Benjamin R. Karney and Thomas N. Bradbury, The Longitudinal Course of Marital Quality and Stability: A Review of Theory, Method, and Research, Psychological Bulletin (1995), 118(1), 3–34. DOI/KEY header is 10.1037/0033-2909.118.1.3. Title/authors/journal/year/pages correspond to the neutral reference (reference uses Methods versus printed Method). This is the cited primary meta-analytic review, with full article sections and references through p.34, not merely an abstract or a secondary report. No PDF was supplied. Target ambiguity: original locator p.17 discusses methods and begins the results section; actual marital-stability aggregates are Figure 1, p.19. Candidates retained only: wives r = -.22 (7 studies), husbands r = -.20 (6 studies); canonical OCR labels read neurotktara and neurobctan, respectively. The p.21 personality discussion identifies the construct as neuroticism/negative affectivity. No sex-specific target is supplied, so neither coefficient is selected. Printed direction is for stability; no reversal to dissolution performed. No single pooled-sex estimate or participant N for these aggregates is supplied in the inspected figure/results methods. Figure 1 reports r and number of studies, without same-aggregate p values or bounds. Generic review totals are not analytic N, and study Ns were not summed because component membership and independence are not established. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders only.
